subject: Economy
theme: chronology of major post-independence economic regulation and institutional establishment in India
question_short_text: Earliest event among banking regulation, insurance nationalization, SBI nationalization, and Five-Year Plan
text:
In the context of independent India's Economy, which one of the following was the earliest event to take place?

a) Nationalisation of Insurance companies
b) Nationalisation of State Bank of India
c) Enactment of Banking Regulation act
d) Introduction of First Five-Year Plan
options: Nationalisation of State Bank of India
explanation: The Banking Regulation Act was enacted in 1949, predating the State Bank of India nationalization (1955), insurance nationalization (1956), and the First Five-Year Plan (1951).

research.summary: This question tests chronological awareness of four pivotal post-independence economic events that shaped India's institutional framework. The Banking Regulation Act came into force on 16 March 1949, making it the earliest among the four options. This Act was crucial legislation passed to consolidate and regulate banking operations after years of banking instability in the pre-independence era, giving the Reserve Bank of India supervisory and regulatory powers over all banking companies in India. The State Bank of India (originally the Imperial Bank of India) was nationalized on 1 July 1955 through the State Bank of India Act, 1955. Life insurance companies were nationalized on 19 January 1956 through an Ordinance, with the Life Insurance Corporation formally constituted on 1 September 1956. The First Five-Year Plan, while often cited as a foundational economic initiative, was introduced in 1951 after the Planning Commission was established in 1950. The critical insight here is that even though the Five-Year Plan is conceptually central to independent India's economic vision, the Banking Regulation Act preceded it by two years. Students often confuse the importance of the Five-Year Plan with its chronological position, but UPSC is testing pure timeline knowledge. The act regulated 1,482 urban and 58 multi-state cooperative banks after later amendments, and became the legislative backbone of India's banking sector governance.
facts: The Banking Regulation Act was passed on 10 March 1949 and came into force on 16 March 1949, before India's formal adoption of the Constitution.
The Imperial Bank of India became the State Bank of India on 1 July 1955, inheriting 480 branches and more than a quarter of India's banking resources at that time.

Life insurance nationalization took place in two stages: management taken over on 19 January 1956 by Ordinance, with formal LIC Act passed on 19 June 1956 and LIC operationalized on 1 September 1956, absorbing 154 Indian, 16 non-Indian insurers and 75 provident societies.
The Planning Commission was established in 1950, with the First Five-Year Plan formally launched in 1951, prioritizing agricultural development and rural India as per the Mahalanobis model.

Before 1949, banking in India was regulated under the Companies Act, 1913, which proved inadequate; the Banking Regulation Act filled this regulatory gap and was subsequently amended in 1965 and 2020 to include cooperative banks.
